messages.author: 12a8430c1bf3f70b
messages.subject: possible bug in density plotting?
parts:
Perhaps it is my mis-understanding, but could the following be a bug in the way density is plotted?  It turns up in this trivial case, but is it more serious beneath the hood?

# trivial data.frame with ten rows
rdf <- structure(list(Times = c(0.0455564993899316, 0.287577520124614,
    0.4089769218117, 0.456614735303447, 0.528105488047004, 0.551435014465824,
    0.788305135443807, 0.883017404004931, 0.892419044394046, 0.940467284293845
    ), Version = structure(c(1L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 3L, 3L,
    3L), .Label = c("1", "2", "3"), class = "factor")), .Names = c("Times",
    "Version"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -10L))
str(rdf)
#'data.frame':    10 obs. of  2 variables:
# $ Times  : num  0.0456 0.2876 0.409 0.4566 0.5281 ...
# $ Version: Factor w/ 3 levels "1","2","3": 1 1 2 3 2 2 2 3 3 3

rdf # clearly has two elements with Version label of 1
#       Times Version
#1  0.0455565       1
#2  0.2875775       1
#3  0.4089769       2
#4  0.4566147       3
#5  0.5281055       2
#6  0.5514350       2
#7  0.7883051       2
#8  0.8830174       3
#9  0.8924190       3
#10 0.9404673       3

library(ggplot2)
qplot(Times, data=rdf, geom='density', colour=Version)
# as seen in ggplot2_density_rdf.png
# here the plot has no apparent trace for Version==1

# as compared with... as seen in density_rdf.png
dev.new()
i <- 1; plot(density(subset(rdf, Version==i)$Times, bw=0.07), lty=i,
             xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,4), main='')
i <- 2; lines(density(subset(rdf, Version==i)$Times, bw=0.07), lty=i)
i <- 3; lines(density(subset(rdf, Version==i)$Times, bw=0.07), lty=i)

# where I can plot a density of the two points
# Yes, this will likely have a different bandwidth,, but should that make a difference?

Is there a minimum count threshold in stat_density() I wonder?

Kind regards,
Sean

There is. There must be at least three cases. It is clearly deliberate
(and has been around for a long time):

https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/commit/a728af0ef98341c9238329c919eb8d6b5bebb7de

But there is nothing in the documentation that states this and no
justification in the code or commit as to why this restriction is there.

There should be a comment about this in the details section of
stat_density, I believe.
